answer: Every claim climbs the copper of verified tasks, and a reviewer at the violet re-runs the work instead of trusting the label. The vault of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. Written in a clipped, no filler register, it stays short. The design leans on escrowed payment for graded work, converted to a slow vesting stream, the unit of trust is a task, not an address. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work.
